advent.label: December 1
advent.title: The Long Wait Begins
advent.passageText: God spoke to the serpent and said that the offspring of the woman would one day crush its head, even as it struck his heel.
advent.reflection: On the worst day in the story, when everything had already broken, God made a promise. Not a fix for that afternoon. A promise that stretched out over thousands of years. We start Advent here, in the wreckage, because that is where the hope was first spoken. God did not wait for things to look good before he promised to set them right.
advent.question: What is something you have been waiting a long time for, and how does the waiting feel?
advent.prayer: God, thank you for keeping promises even when we cannot see how. Help us wait with you.

advent.label: December 2
advent.title: A Family for the World
advent.passageText: God told Abram to leave his country and go to a land he would be shown, and said that through Abram all the families of the earth would be blessed.
advent.reflection: Abram was old and had no children, and God told him his family would bless the whole world. That is a strange thing to promise an old man with an empty house. But the rescue God planned was not going to drop out of the sky. It was going to come through a family, through ordinary people who said yes when they could not see the end. We are part of that long line tonight.
advent.question: What would it feel like to follow God somewhere without a map?
advent.prayer: God, give us the courage of Abram to go where you lead us.

advent.label: December 3
advent.title: God Hears in the Dark
advent.passageText: God said he had seen the suffering of his people in Egypt and heard their cry, and that he had come down to rescue them.
advent.reflection: The people had been slaves for four hundred years. Four hundred years is longer than the United States has existed. For all that time it must have looked like God was not listening. Then he says, I have seen, I have heard, I have come down. God was not absent in those long years. He was working in a way too slow for anyone to feel. Advent teaches us that God being quiet is not the same as God being gone.
advent.question: Have you ever felt like no one was listening to you? What helped?
advent.prayer: God, thank you that you hear us even when we feel forgotten.

advent.label: December 4
advent.title: A King Who Lasts
advent.passageText: God promised King David that one of his descendants would have a kingdom that would last forever.
advent.reflection: David was a real king with a real throne, and God told him a son from his line would reign forever. No human king lasts forever. They get old, they fail, they die. So this promise pointed past David, past all the kings who came after, toward someone the world had not met yet. Every Christmas card with a manger in it is the answer to a promise made to a shepherd boy who became a king.
advent.question: What makes someone a good leader, in your eyes?
advent.prayer: Jesus, thank you for being a king whose kingdom never ends.

advent.label: December 5
advent.title: Out of Bethlehem
advent.passageText: The prophet said that out of Bethlehem, small among the towns of Judah, would come one who would rule over Israel, whose beginnings were from long ago.
advent.reflection: Bethlehem was a small town, the kind of place people drove past on the way to somewhere bigger. And God circled it on the map hundreds of years early. He does not pick the way we pick. We look for the big stage and the bright lights. God looked at a town nobody noticed and said, there. If you have ever felt small or overlooked, pay attention to where God chose to begin.
advent.question: Why do you think God so often chooses small and quiet things?
advent.prayer: God, thank you that you notice small places and small people.

advent.label: December 6
advent.title: A Child Is Given
advent.passageText: Isaiah said that to us a child is born, to us a son is given, and the government would rest on his shoulders, and he would be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
advent.reflection: Isaiah said these words seven hundred years before the first Christmas. He had never seen a manger. He was writing in a frightened country surrounded by armies, and into that fear he said, a child is coming, and he will carry the whole weight of the world on his shoulders. Notice that the rescue arrives as a baby. The strongest thing God ever did, he did as someone who could not yet hold up his own head.
advent.question: Which of those names for Jesus means the most to you tonight, and why?
advent.prayer: Jesus, you are the Prince of Peace. Bring your peace into our home.

advent.label: December 7
advent.title: A Light in Deep Darkness
advent.passageText: Isaiah said the people walking in darkness had seen a great light, and on those living in the land of deep shadow a light had dawned.
advent.reflection: Isaiah did not pretend the darkness was not real. He called it deep, he called it shadow, he did not soften it. That is honest, and we should be honest too. Some seasons are dark. Some families this December are missing someone at the table. The promise is not that the dark is fake. The promise is that a light is coming into it, and the dark has never once been able to put it out.
advent.question: Where in the world, or in our family, do we most need light right now?
advent.prayer: God, shine your light into the dark places we cannot fix ourselves.

advent.label: December 8
advent.title: A Branch from a Stump
advent.passageText: Isaiah said a shoot would come up from the stump of Jesse, and a branch would bear fruit from his roots.
advent.reflection: A stump is what is left after a tree gets cut down. It looks finished, dead, done. Israel had been cut down to a stump, the old royal family reduced to almost nothing. And Isaiah looked at the stump and saw a green shoot pushing up through the bark. God does his best work where we have already given up. The family that looked dead was about to grow the most important branch in history.
advent.question: Have you ever seen something come back to life that you thought was over?
advent.prayer: God, thank you for bringing new life out of dead places.

advent.label: December 9
advent.title: Comfort My People
advent.passageText: Isaiah heard the words, comfort, comfort my people, and a voice calling to prepare in the wilderness a way for the Lord.
advent.reflection: After many hard chapters, God says one word twice. Comfort, comfort. He is not embarrassed to comfort his people. Some of us were taught that strong people do not need comfort, that we should toughen up and stop needing things. God does not talk to us that way. He bends down. He speaks gently to the worn out. Advent is God preparing a road to come close to people who are tired.
advent.question: What is the most comforting thing someone has ever said to you?
advent.prayer: God, thank you that you come close and speak gently to us.

advent.label: December 10
advent.title: The Servant Who Carries It
advent.passageText: Isaiah said he took up our pain and bore our suffering, and he was pierced for our wrongs and crushed for our failures, and by his wounds we are healed.
advent.reflection: This is the strangest promise of Advent. The one who is coming will not just rule, he will suffer. He will carry our pain on his own back. Most of us spend our lives trying to put down what is heavy. Jesus walked into the world to pick up everything heavy and carry it himself. When we hang ornaments and sing songs, we should not forget that the baby was born to do the hardest thing anyone has ever done.
advent.question: What is something heavy you wish someone would help you carry?
advent.prayer: Jesus, thank you for carrying what was too heavy for us.

advent.label: December 11
advent.title: A New Heart
advent.passageText: God promised to give his people a new heart and put a new spirit in them, and to remove the heart of stone and give a heart of flesh.
advent.reflection: God did not promise to give us better rules. He promised to give us new hearts. There is a difference. A rule tells you what to do on the outside. A new heart changes what you want on the inside. We all know how it feels to do the right thing while wanting the wrong thing. God says, I will go deeper than that. The baby coming at Christmas came to do heart surgery on the whole human race.
advent.question: What is the difference between obeying because you have to and obeying because you want to?
advent.prayer: God, give us soft hearts that want what is good.

advent.label: December 12
advent.title: How Long, O Lord
advent.passageText: David asked the Lord how long he would be forgotten, how long God would hide his face, how long he must wrestle with his thoughts and sorrow in his heart.
advent.reflection: Even in Advent, full of promises, the people of God asked hard questions out loud. How long. Where are you. David put these questions right into a song he sang in worship. That tells us something. You are allowed to bring your real questions to God. He is not fragile. The waiting of Advent is not always pretty, and God would rather hear our honest ache than our pretend calm.
advent.question: Is there a question you have wanted to ask God but felt afraid to?
advent.prayer: God, thank you that we can bring you our hardest questions.

advent.label: December 13
advent.title: The Messenger Comes First
advent.passageText: God said he would send his messenger to prepare the way before him, and then the Lord they were seeking would suddenly come to his temple.
advent.reflection: Malachi is the last book before a long silence. After he spoke, four hundred years passed with no prophet, no new word. Imagine waiting four hundred years for a sentence to finish. Then a man named John showed up in the wilderness, the messenger Malachi promised, and the silence broke. God is never late, even when he is slow enough to make us wonder if he forgot.
advent.question: What is the hardest part of waiting when you do not know how long it will be?
advent.prayer: God, help us trust you even in the long quiet times.

advent.label: December 14
advent.title: An Old Man Hears Good News
advent.passageText: An angel told Zechariah not to be afraid, because his prayer had been heard and his wife Elizabeth would have a son, and they would name him John.
advent.reflection: Zechariah and Elizabeth were old and had prayed for a child for years with no answer. They had probably stopped expecting one. Then God answered a prayer they had nearly given up on. Sometimes the answer comes so late we have forgotten we asked. God was not ignoring them in all those years. He was lining up the moment when their son would announce the Savior of the world.
advent.question: Is there something you prayed for once and then stopped expecting?
advent.prayer: God, thank you that you remember our prayers even when we forget them.

advent.label: December 15
advent.title: Let It Be
advent.passageText: Mary said to the angel that she was the servant of the Lord, and that it should happen to her just as he had said.
advent.reflection: Mary was young, probably a teenager, and the angel asked her to carry the Son of God, which would turn her whole life upside down. She had every reason to be afraid of what people would say. She said yes anyway. Not because it was easy or safe, but because she trusted the God who asked. Saying yes to God almost never means saying yes to the comfortable thing.
advent.question: What is something hard you think God might be asking you to say yes to?
advent.prayer: God, give us the trust of Mary to say yes when it is hard.

advent.label: December 16
advent.title: The Lowly Lifted
advent.passageText: Mary sang that God had brought down rulers from their thrones but lifted up the humble, and had filled the hungry with good things but sent the rich away empty.
advent.reflection: When Mary found out what God was doing, she did not sing a quiet little lullaby. She sang about a world turned upside down, where the proud get knocked off their thrones and the forgotten get a seat at the table. This is what Christmas means. God is not coming to make the powerful more powerful. He is coming for the people the world walks past. That should comfort some of us and unsettle the rest of us.
advent.question: How is God's way of measuring greatness different from the world's way?
advent.prayer: God, thank you for noticing the people everyone else ignores.

advent.label: December 17
advent.title: Joseph Stays
advent.passageText: An angel told Joseph in a dream not to be afraid to take Mary as his wife, because the child she carried was from the Holy Spirit, and he would save his people from their sins.
advent.reflection: Joseph could have walked away, and no one would have blamed him. Instead he stayed, took on a son who was not his by blood, and raised the Savior of the world in a carpenter shop. We do not have a single word Joseph said recorded anywhere. We only have what he did. Sometimes the most faithful thing a person ever does is quietly stay and take care of people who need them.
advent.question: Who has quietly stayed and taken care of you?
advent.prayer: God, help us be people who stay and care for others like Joseph did.

advent.label: December 18
advent.title: The Word Was God
advent.passageText: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God, and through him all things were made.
advent.reflection: Before Bethlehem, before the manger, before there was a sky to hang stars in, Jesus already was. The baby in the straw was not the beginning of him. He made the trees that the manger was cut from. He made the lungs that took his own first breath. The wonder of Christmas is not just that a baby was born. It is that the One who made everything chose to become small enough to be held.
advent.question: What is the biggest thing you can imagine that Jesus made?
advent.prayer: Jesus, thank you that the maker of everything came to be with us.

advent.label: December 19
advent.title: The Word Moved In
advent.passageText: The Word became flesh and made his home among us, and we have seen his glory, full of grace and truth.
advent.reflection: God did not save us from far away with a wave of his hand. He moved into the neighborhood. He got skin and hunger and tired feet. He learned to walk and got splinters and felt the cold. When you love someone, you do not stay at a safe distance. You come close. This is how close God was willing to come. He moved in.
advent.question: What does it mean to you that God wanted to be near us, not far away?
advent.prayer: God, thank you for coming close instead of staying far away.

advent.label: December 20
advent.title: No Room
advent.passageText: While they were in Bethlehem the time came for the baby to be born, and Mary wrapped him in cloths and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn.
advent.reflection: The King of the universe was born in a place where animals ate, because no one had a room for him. From his very first night, Jesus knew what it was to be turned away. If you have ever felt like there was no place for you, like you did not fit anywhere, look at the manger. He started there on purpose. He came to the people the world had no room for.
advent.question: Have you ever felt like there was no room for you somewhere? How did it feel?
advent.prayer: Jesus, thank you for making room for us when the world would not.

advent.label: December 21
advent.title: Good News for Shepherds
advent.passageText: The angel told the shepherds not to be afraid, because he brought good news of great joy for all people, that a Savior had been born in the town of David.
advent.reflection: When God announced the most important birth in history, he did not send the news to kings or to the temple. He sent it to shepherds working the night shift in a field. Shepherds were poor, dirty, and looked down on. They were the last people anyone expected to get an invitation. That is the heart of Christmas. The good news goes first to the people who are used to being last.
advent.question: Why do you think the angels told the shepherds first?
advent.prayer: God, thank you for bringing good news to ordinary people like us.

advent.label: December 22
advent.title: Mary Treasured It
advent.passageText: Mary treasured all these things and pondered them in her heart.
advent.reflection: After the shepherds left and the noise died down, Mary did not rush on to the next thing. She held it all quietly and turned it over in her heart. We live in a hurry, and December can become a blur of lights and lists and noise. Mary slows us down. Some things are too big to talk about right away. Some things you just hold and let sink in. This is one of them.
advent.question: What is something good in your life you want to slow down and treasure?
advent.prayer: God, help us slow down and treasure the good things you give us.

advent.label: December 23
advent.title: A Light to Everyone
advent.passageText: Old Simeon held the baby and said his eyes had seen God's salvation, a light to the nations and the glory of God's people Israel.
advent.reflection: Simeon was old and had waited his whole life to see God keep his promise. When he finally held the baby Jesus, he said he could die in peace now. Imagine waiting your entire life for one moment and then having it placed in your arms. The promise made all the way back in the garden, carried through Abraham and David and the prophets, was now small enough to hold. The long wait was nearly over.
advent.question: What is something you would be willing to wait your whole life for?
advent.prayer: God, thank you for keeping every promise you ever made.

advent.label: December 24
advent.title: The Night Before
advent.passageText: In those days a decree went out that all the world should be counted, and Joseph went up from Nazareth to Bethlehem with Mary, who was expecting a child.
advent.reflection: On the night before everything changed, a tired couple was walking a hard road because a faraway emperor wanted to count people for taxes. They had no idea they were walking straight into the center of the whole story. Most world changing things do not feel grand while they are happening. They feel like a long, ordinary, tiring day. Tonight we wait the way they waited, on the edge of something we cannot fully see yet.
advent.question: What are you most looking forward to about tomorrow?
advent.prayer: God, as we wait tonight, fill our hearts with quiet hope.

advent.label: December 25
advent.title: He Is Here
advent.passageText: Today in the town of David a Savior has been born to you, who is Christ the Lord.
advent.reflection: Today. After Genesis and the garden, after Abraham and David, after Isaiah and the long silence, after Mary and Joseph and the road to Bethlehem, the word is today. The promise made in the dark at the start of the story is keeping itself in a manger. God is no longer only a promise. God is here, with skin and breath, in a body that can be held. Every wait we have ever waited points to this. He came. He is still coming for us. Merry Christmas.
advent.question: Now that he is here, what do you most want to say to Jesus today?
advent.prayer: Jesus, thank you for coming. We are so glad you are here with us.

holyWeek.label: Palm Sunday
holyWeek.title: The Wrong Kind of King
holyWeek.passageText: A huge crowd spread their coats on the road and waved branches, shouting Hosanna to the Son of David, blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.
holyWeek.reflection: The crowd wanted a king who would ride in on a war horse and throw out the Romans. Jesus came in on a young donkey, slow and humble, the way kings came when they came in peace. The people cheered, but most of them were cheering for a king they had made up in their heads, not the one actually in front of them. By Friday the same crowd would turn on him. It is easy to cheer for the Jesus we wish we had. It is harder to follow the one who is really there.
holyWeek.question: Have you ever wanted Jesus to do things your way instead of his way?
holyWeek.prayer: Jesus, help us love you as you really are, not as we wish you were.

holyWeek.label: Monday
holyWeek.title: Turning Over the Tables
holyWeek.passageText: Jesus went into the temple and drove out those buying and selling, saying that his house was meant to be a house of prayer but they had made it a den of robbers.
holyWeek.reflection: The temple was supposed to be the one place where anyone could come close to God, and people had turned it into a marketplace where the poor got cheated. Jesus got angry, and his anger was right. We sometimes think Jesus was gentle about everything. He was not. He cared so much about people getting to God that he flipped tables to clear the way. Love that never gets angry at what hurts people is not really love.
holyWeek.question: What kinds of things do you think make Jesus angry, and why?
holyWeek.prayer: Jesus, thank you for caring enough to clear away what keeps us from God.

holyWeek.label: Tuesday
holyWeek.title: The Greatest Command
holyWeek.passageText: Jesus said to love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, and mind, and to love your neighbor as yourself, and that all the law hangs on these two commands.
holyWeek.reflection: People kept trying to trap Jesus with hard questions that week, hoping he would say something they could arrest him for. He kept answering with the truth instead. When asked which rule mattered most, he gave two, and tied them together. Love God. Love people. Everything else is just figuring out how to do those two things. It sounds simple until you try to love someone who is hard to love. Then you find out it is the work of a lifetime.
holyWeek.question: Who is someone in your life that is hard to love, and what would loving them look like?
holyWeek.prayer: God, help us love you with everything and love the people around us.

holyWeek.label: Wednesday
holyWeek.title: A Friend Walks Away
holyWeek.passageText: Judas, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests and asked what they would give him to hand Jesus over, and they paid him thirty pieces of silver.
holyWeek.reflection: Judas had walked with Jesus for three years. He had seen the miracles, eaten the meals, heard every word. And he sold his friend for a bag of silver. We like to think we are nothing like Judas, but every one of us has chosen something small over someone who loved us. Wednesday is a hard, quiet day in the story. It reminds us that betrayal does not always come from strangers. Sometimes it comes from people who were very close.
holyWeek.question: Why do you think someone who knew Jesus so well would still turn away?
holyWeek.prayer: God, keep our hearts close to you so we do not drift away.

holyWeek.label: Maundy Thursday
holyWeek.title: Bread, Cup, and Basin
holyWeek.passageText: Jesus said that if he, their Lord and teacher, had washed their feet, they should also wash one another's feet, for he had given them an example to follow.
holyWeek.reflection: On his last night, Jesus took off his outer robe, knelt down, and washed the dirty feet of his friends, a job usually left to the lowest servant. Then he gave them bread and a cup and told them to remember him. The God of the universe knelt at the feet of fishermen. If that is how the greatest one acted, then greatness in his family will always look like serving, never like being served. Real love kneels down.
holyWeek.question: What is a way you could serve someone in our family this week?
holyWeek.prayer: Jesus, thank you for kneeling down to serve us. Help us serve others.

holyWeek.label: Good Friday
holyWeek.title: It Is Finished
holyWeek.passageText: When Jesus had received the drink, he said it is finished, and he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.
holyWeek.reflection: This is the hardest day, and we should not rush past it. Jesus, who had done nothing wrong, was nailed to a cross and died. We call it good, which seems strange for a day with so much pain in it. It is good because he was carrying our wrong, not his own. When he said it is finished, he did not mean his life was over and he had lost. He meant the work was done. The rescue planned since the garden was complete. Let today feel heavy. It was.
holyWeek.question: Why do you think we call such a sad day Good Friday?
holyWeek.prayer: Jesus, thank you for loving us all the way to the cross.

holyWeek.label: Holy Saturday
holyWeek.title: The Day of Silence
holyWeek.passageText: Joseph took the body, wrapped it in clean linen, laid it in his own new tomb, rolled a great stone across the entrance, and went away.
holyWeek.reflection: Saturday is the day nobody talks about much. Jesus was in the tomb, and his friends did not know yet that Sunday was coming. They only knew their hope was dead and buried behind a stone. We all have Saturdays, days stuck between something terrible and something we cannot yet see. If you are in one, you are in good company. The friends of Jesus sat in that silence too, and the best news in history was already on its way to them.
holyWeek.question: What do you do when you have to wait and you cannot see what comes next?
holyWeek.prayer: God, when we are stuck in the waiting, help us trust that you are still working.

holyWeek.label: Easter Sunday
holyWeek.title: He Is Not Here
holyWeek.passageText: The angel told the women not to be afraid, for Jesus who was crucified was not there, because he had risen, just as he said.
holyWeek.reflection: The women came to the tomb in the dark, expecting to care for a dead body. Instead they found the stone rolled away and the grave empty. He had risen. Death, the one enemy nobody beats, had been beaten. This is why Christians have never stopped celebrating for two thousand years. The promise from the very first page of the story, that the darkness would be crushed, came true on a Sunday morning. He is alive. And because he lives, the worst thing is never the last thing.
holyWeek.question: What does it change for us that Jesus is alive and not still in the tomb?
holyWeek.prayer: Jesus, you are alive. Thank you for beating death so we never have to fear it.
